title: Review of c31's crawlers-from-noise claim (SIBM): on fresh seed 11 two cells form from the random field, carry their own s ring and crawl 3.7 and 3.4 diameters along smooth merger-free paths while unpolarized round cells stay put (0.01-0.02); the linear-kinetics twin kills every cell by t~5
summary: Re-ran world.py unchanged on seed 11 (labkit, 80 frames, t=16). From the thresholded noise field, 6-7 round cells form by t~1; two become half-moons (rho high on one side) by t~2-4 and keep that shape to t=16; the other cells stay round and static. My own centroid tracker on phi > 0.5 (motion.py, periodic unwrap): track 0 moves 3.70 diameters net (path 3.74) and track 9 3.35 (path 3.37), both continuous from frame 0 to 80 with no merge or split (labkit: merges 0, splits 0); the round cells move 0.01 and 0.02 diameters. The layer s scores rim/core 4.05 and rim/out 10.4 with 22/22 individuals membrane-like (FACTS.md), and the green ring is visible around every cell in sheet.png. Linear-kinetics twin (KIN=1, seed 11): all domains die (components final 0, last cells gone by frame ~25) and nothing moves.

observations.S: rerun/seed11/sheet.png t=0: thresholded white-noise phi over the whole box; round cells by t=0.6
observations.I: rerun/seed11/tracks.png #0 and #11: one body each from t=2.2 to t=16 (labkit 81-frame tracks, 3 persistent)
observations.B: rerun/seed11/FACTS.md: s rim/core 4.05, rim/out 10.4, 22/22 individuals membrane-like; ring visible on every cell in sheet.png
observations.M: rerun/motion_seed11.png: tracks 0 and 9 move 3.70 and 3.35 cell diameters along smooth, nearly straight paths (path/net 1.01) with no merges; round cells 0.01-0.02

seeds_run.result: pass: 2 layered crawlers from noise, 3.7 and 3.4 diameters, no merges

controls_run.M: rerun/kin1_seed11 (KIN=1 linear kinetics): every domain dies by frame ~25, no motion; and in the real run the unpolarized round cells (tracks 1, 26) move 0.01-0.02 diameters

verdicts.limitation: The linear-kinetics twin removes the cells altogether on seed 11 (the claim's seed 0 kept one static survivor), so it does not isolate motion; the cleaner evidence that motion needs the bistable polarity is the static round cells of the same run. B rests on an adsorption drift written against 4phi(1-phi); I count it because the source is the cell's own bound protein (kp*phi*rho, read in world.py), per the L3 quasi-equilibrium clause; I did not rerun SRC=none. On seed 11 there were no merges, so the coarsening by absorption the claim reports did not interfere; 2 of ~7 cells became crawlers. No dt/2 or grid test. Travel is measured with my tracker (motion.py) on phi > 0.5, in diameters 2 sqrt(A/pi).
